newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Communist urges parliament to make Yeltsin quit.
newsitem.headline: Communist urges parliament to make Yeltsin quit.

text.p: A leading communist lawmaker urged the Russian parliament on Tuesday to force President Boris Yeltsin out of office because of his persistent ill health.
Viktor Ilyukhin said the State Duma's security committee, which he chairs, had agreed the initiative after heated debate.

The initiative will be discussed by the Duma's legal department, but it has virtually no chance of unseating the president. The speaker of the lower house, fellow communist Gennady Seleznyov, told reporters the proposal was unlikely to be put to parliamentary party groups for at least a week.

Alexander Kotenkov, Yeltsin's representative in the Duma, said the move had no legislative basis and was simply an attempt to stir up "political scandal". He said only the president could decide whether his own health was too weak to remain in office.
Yeltsin came down with pneumonia just two weeks after returning to the Kremlin following his heart bypass operation on November 5, and he has been in hospital since last Wednesday.

Parliament has little power to oust the president under the 1993 constitution, which puts vast authority in the hands of the head of state. Although the communists are the biggest party in the Duma, it is unlikely they could build the overwhelming majority needed to impeach Yeltsin.
